## The Soul Seeks Salvation and Sanctification in GOD.

Lord! You who with a single word can fell mighty powers,
Who—whatever stirs against You with an impudent mind—
Often lays it in the dust in the blink of an eye:
Be to my poor soul like firm walls and ramparts,
Which can repel the fury of my enemies!
When the world now pitches its camp against me,
Then pay it back with the coin forever stamped for it, <note>Likely an allusion to the "wages of sin" or the biblical concept of rendering unto the world what belongs to it.</note>
And cast it in Your wrath to the very threshold of the abyss!
Only You, O great GOD! occupy <image-desc>heart symbol</image-desc> and senses,
Grant that they may be Your stool and throne-seat!
Deign to call my mind Your temple-house:
Let my conscience be the Holy of Holies, <note>original: "Allerheiligste" — referring to the innermost sanctuary of the Tabernacle or Temple, where the presence of God resided.</note>
Keep this always pure for Your glory, like gold,
So that the world will no longer be able to approach me!

## Conclusion.

What then is the world now, and what in it boasts so much?
Nothing but a hollow nothing, a soon-discarded carcass; <note>original: "Aas" — literally carrion; a common Baroque metaphor for the decaying and transient nature of physical existence.</note>
A shadow that only paints vain vapors before us,
A cold-frozen ice and soon-shattering glass;
A mirror that cunningly blinds the fickle senses,
A dungeon of true rest that disturbs our freedom:
A will-o'-the-wisp <note>original: "Irrwisch" — a ghost-light or atmospheric flame that leads travelers off the path into marshes.</note> that seduces and turns us from the truth,
A magic show that perverts our mind and understanding;
A fairground where one finds nothing but false wares,
A fishhook <note>original: "Angel" — here used metaphorically for the lure that pulls a soul into destruction.</note> that only tears us into ruin;
An <image-desc>executioner symbol</image-desc> servant who binds us in chains and fetters,
Who steals our freedom and points us toward the prison:
And who would have the patience to count all the names
Which this child of a harlot <note>The "World" was frequently personified as a seductive prostitute (the Whore of Babylon) in 17th-century devotional literature.</note> has given itself?
Blessed is he whom its burden can no longer torment,
Nor bears its evil mark on his forehead and <image-desc>hand symbol</image-desc>! <note>A reference to the "Mark of the Beast" from the Book of Revelation, signifying those who belong to the world rather than God.</note>
One truly must not call it a game or pastime,
When one is led away as a slave during a robbery:
Still less can one recognize it as a pleasure,
When the yoke of the earth adorns a free <image-desc>neck symbol</image-desc>.

# Appendix of Poetic Poems.

He who must [serve] on galleys in hard bonds and iron,
Constantly pulling the heavy oars amidst plenty of blows,
And tearing through wild waves in the harsh storm,
Need not trouble himself to boast of his fortune.
Yet he who has put his neck into the yoke of the world,
And carries its hundred-weight burden <note>original: "Centner-Last" — a "Zentner" was a heavy unit of weight (approx. 50kg/110lbs), here used to symbolize the crushing gravity of worldly concerns.</note> upon his shoulders,
Is tethered to an even harder yoke and misery,
And far more pitiably overwhelmed with burdens.
Therefore, he who in earnest wishes to become a free master,
And be unassailed by distressing weights,
Let him tear his spirit <note>original: "Gemüth" — the seat of emotions and thought, often translated as soul or mind.</note> away from the heavy yoke of the earth,
And turn heart and mind only toward heaven.
There one can surely build firm dwellings;
Here <note>The poet refers to heaven as "here" to signify the spiritual presence of God.</note> no grim enemy nor tyranny is known:
Here one can entrust what they have quite free of worry;
Here one knows nothing at all of inconstancy.
Now, God, open the wide gates of heaven to me!
I hurry out of the world and take up residence with You.
Because it has pleased You to lead me into rest,
I will now henceforth be forever at peace in You!

Love love and piety; <note>original: "Frömmigkeit" — a central Lutheran concept involving both inward faith and outward religious practice.</note>
Praise the LORD in purity;
Live in peace and unity /
Do good to all / and harm to none;
Then, before both God and men,
Both now in time and in eternity,
You shall be praiseworthy <note>original: "Ruhmwürdig" — literally "worthy of fame/glory," though in this context it implies a reputation for holiness.</note> and truly blessed!

---

## In Praise of Humility.

Humility is good for everything,
Without humility, no one does good;
Humility is a noble virtue,
It suits the elderly / and adorns the youth;
Humility springs from God’s love,
Humility enters into God through love,
Humility brings love down again,
Blessed is the one / who strives for humility,
Everything succeeds well for them!

---

## A Little Sigh. <note>original: "Seuffzerlein" — a popular Baroque term for a short, spontaneous, and fervent prayer, often intended to be memorized and recited throughout the day.</note>

LORD / you who are near to me,
Let me obtain grace,
To receive humility /
Which is your gift /
From You,
->AMEN!<-

<vocab>Piety, Purity, Unity, Humility, Virtue, Little Sigh (Brief Prayer)</vocab>

## Printing Errors.

Sheet 84, Line 21, read: *their*. Sheet 247, Lines 8 and 9, for: "from the spirit, according to the will and through the grace of man," read thus: "from the will of the first man, or according to the flesh, but solely from the spirit, according to the will and through the grace of **G**OD." <note>This correction is theologically significant, shifting the agency of salvation or spiritual action from humanity to God.</note>

--- Page 675 ---
<meta>This page provides a conceptual map or "threefold table" of the author's entire theological system. It acts as a bridge between the table of contents and the main body of the work, summarizing the core dualities of the author’s thought: flesh versus spirit, the two Adams, and the letter of the law versus the living spirit of faith.</meta>

# Content and Brief Concept
## Of the Entire Theology /
### or also
### Of the Entire Holy Scripture / Old and New Testaments / and all Acts of GOD /
-> arranged into a threefold table: <-
-> By the same Author. <-

---

### I.
#### Christ / the Son of GOD / and Seed of Abraham / is the End / and Fulfillment / of the Law / the Prophets / and all Promises of GOD.

<image-desc>A logical diagram using braces to show two paths of fulfillment: the path of the flesh and the path of the spirit.</image-desc>

*   **[Shadow <note>original: "Umbra"</note>]** — **Flesh** — are in the **Figure / Bodily Temporal Truth** — Promises made to his descendants: Isaac and Israel according to the flesh: — **Flesh:** — hence is the People of the **Old Testament / namely the Jews:** — to these belong **Moses together with the Law** — **[Shadow <note>original: "Schatten"</note>]** and all its belongings.
*   **[Truth <note>original: "Veritas"</note>]** — **Spirit** — are in the **Spiritual Eternal Truth** — **Spirit:** — hence is the People of the **New Testament / namely the Christians:** — to these belong **Christ together with the Gospel** — **[Truth <note>original: "Wahrheit"</note>]**

---

### II.
#### Contrast and Origin of the two ADAMS:
-> Of the First / from the Earth <image-desc>floral cross symbol</image-desc> Of the Other from Heaven. <-

<image-desc>A logical diagram contrasting the first Adam (death) and the second Adam (life) through their origins, nature, offspring, and spiritual state.</image-desc>

*   **[Death <note>original: "Mors"</note>]** — The **First ADAM** is from the **Earth / earthly / an old dead human before GOD.** — hence he then / as he is / **bears earthly dead fruits and children / who also because of the First Birth** — from **Flesh; are fleshly / old / corrupted / hated / rejected humans and children / of Damnation and Death /** — upon whom all **Disgrace / Wrath and Anger [Death] of GOD the Most High remains eternally.**
*   **[Life <note>original: "Vita"</note>]** — The **Other ADAM** is from **Heaven / heavenly / a new living human before GOD.** — hence he then / as he is / **bears heavenly living fruits and children / who also because of the Other or Rebirth** — from **Spirit; are spiritual / newly born / beloved / chosen humans and children / of Salvation and eternal Life /** — upon whom all **Grace / Goodness and Love [Life] of GOD the Most High remains eternally.**

---

### III.
#### Contrast and Origin of the historical false and righteous saving Faith.

<image-desc>A logical diagram contrasting historical faith based on the "letter" and living faith based on the "spirit."</image-desc>

*   **[Letter <note>original: "Litera"</note>]** — An **historical dead faith comes from the hearing of the external written Word of GOD / which is learned in the school of men / and heard with the outward ears of the flesh:** — Hence then come **the scribes and ministers of the letter / together with their calling and mission. [Letter <note>original: "Buchstabe"</note>]**
*   **[Spirit <note>original: "Spiritus"</note>]** — A **living true faith comes from the hearing of the internal eternal Word of GOD / which is learned in the school of the Holy Spirit / and heard with the inward ears of the spirit:** — Hence then come **the divines <note>translated from "Gottesgelehrten," referring to those taught directly by God rather than by human institutions</note> and ministers of the spirit / together with their calling and mission. [Spirit <note>original: "Geist"</note>]**

---

-> Whoever now does not understand this / nor wishes to understand / <-
-> he is a person of confused senses / a builder of Babylon <note>A reference to the Tower of Babel, symbolizing spiritual confusion and prideful human effort.</note> / and a misleader of the ignorant people / <-
-> unfit either to teach / or to distinguish the wholesome teaching. <-

---

-> Summary of Summaries / it remains thus: <-
> That which is born of the flesh is flesh; and that which is born of the Spirit is spirit. <note>original: John 3:6</note>

-> Therefore do not marvel at what the eternal Truth, Christ JESUS, regarding it as the highest necessity, has said: <-
> **You must be born again or from above!** <note>original: John 3:7</note>

<vocab>Theology, Promises, Shadow, Truth, Death, Life, Letter, Spirit, Adam, Rebirth, Scribes, Divines</vocab>

<summary>This page presents a "threefold table" summarizing the work's theology, contrasting the carnal/historical understanding of religion with a spiritual/living experience of faith. It emphasizes the necessity of the "New Birth" and distinguishes between the "First Adam" of earthly death and the "Second Adam" of heavenly life.</summary>
<keywords>Theology, New Birth, Adam, Flesh vs. Spirit, Shadow and Truth, Historical Faith, Scribes, Holy Spirit, salvation, Law and Gospel</keywords>
